newsitem.title: USA: Versace house joins grisly roster of murder sites.
newsitem.headline: Versace house joins grisly roster of murder sites.

text.p: As a firefighter hosed blood from the stone steps of the mansion where he was murdered on Tuesday, Gianni Versace's Miami Beach mansion joined the grisly roster of America's celebrity murder sites.
Three red roses lay on the sidewalk a few feet from the steps where Versace died. Red-tinged water ran from the steps into a gutter.
Across the street, a plastic cup of red roses sat on the sidewalk and a bouquet of flowers was propped against a parking meter. Hundreds of people gathered and talked quietly.

With the daylight murder of the Italian fashion icon just hours old, the scene at Versace's renovated mansion among the pastel-hued Art Deco hotels of the city's South Beach district recalled the Los Angeles townhouse where Nicole Brown Simpson was killed in 1994, or the sidewalk outside New York's Dakota apartment building where John Lennon was slain in 1980.

"It's very sad. Versace was to the fashion world what John Lennon was to music," said John Winarski, 35, a South Beach resident who went to the scene out of curiosity. "I think Miami Beach will suffer from this. This was a worldwide personality."

Models on Rollerblades, tourists in bathing suits, residents in shorts and T-shirts, the old and young gathered to lament the violent death of Versace, who was shot twice in the head as he returned home from breakfast at a restaurant nearby. Police said he appeared to have been targeted.

"It's unbelievable. The guy always walked around the streets. He was so peaceful," said Rachel Tudela, 23, a resident of glitzy South Beach, a beachfront tourist and model mecca where Versace made his part-time home.
The crime scene stopped tourists in their tracks.

"We saw all the blood on the stairs," said Katrina Froyland, 21, a visitor from Norway. "It's scary, really scary. We had heard that bad things happen in Miami. We are going to be really careful now."

Tourists and locals alike shot video and snapped photos of the gated mansion with its red, barrel-tiled roof, cream-coloured walls and surrounding palms and evergreen bushes. Versace spent millions to renovate and expand the old apartment building into a sparkling Mediterranean-style villa.
"My neighbours told me of his death. I wanted to see his house where he was for the last time," said resident Lolimar Bazam, 27, eyes tearing.
Bazam, a Venezuelan who lives nearby, rushed across the street to snap pictures of the mansion's entrance when police took down their yellow-tape barricade.
"I am very sad. He was very important to the community. Gianni Versace was very good for the people."
